thread:
Lena: Quick follow-up to yesterday's onboarding RFC. Proposing a thin 'admit-probe' stage that runs static+micro runtime checks before models enter the full bench queue. Aim: reduce wasted GPU bench runs and speed feedback to model owners. Thoughts?

Ravi: Sounds promising. How thin is 'thin'? We need to budget cost; benches are expensive but probes must be cheap and deterministic.

Omar: Proposed probe components: 1) static fingerprint (op multiset + dtype/shape signatures), 2) lightweight kernel microbench (single matmul + elementwise), 3) tiny smoke generation (max 8 tokens) only for ambiguous fingerprints. Keep each step capped in time.

Priya: We should be explicit about false-positive risk, especially for community converters that reorder ops. Suggest we prefer under-rejection: if uncertain, escalate to bench rather than reject.

Lena: Agreed on conservative stance. Probe should return ACCEPT / ESCALATE / REJECT. REJECT only for clear ABI/kernel missing or failing microbench. ESCALATE queues for full bench.

Ravi: Instrumentation needed: probe.latency_p50/p95, probe.accept_rate_by_model_family, probe.escalation_ratio, probe.reject_reasons. Also bench.false_accept_after_probe metric.

Omar: For static fingerprinting, multiset approach avoids ordering issues. Use canonicalized op-id + param-shape-hash and sort to build fingerprint string. Also include 'kv_schema_stamp' since KV cache schema changes are frequent cause of bustage.

Priya: UX: Authors should get machine-readable rejection details and a link to a one-click reproduce bundle. That'll cut triage time. Also dry-run mode in the SDK for authors to run locally before submission.

Lena: Rollout plan: alpha for internal model teams first, then opens to partners. Start by marking probe as advisory (no automatic block) for 2 weeks, compare probe decisions vs bench outcomes, tune thresholds.

Ravi: Operational guardrails: daily probe budget, per-author rate limits, and circuit-breaker if probe error rate spikes. We should cap microbench CPU/GPU time per probe to avoid DoS via malicious model uploads.

Omar: Microbench details: run matmul of dims (64x128)x(128x64) single iteration on the same device type as bench pool but with reduced precision config, measure median of 3 runs. Compare to expected range for family+quant. If >3x slower -> KERNEL_FALLBACK and REJECT.

Priya: We also need a small blacklist/whitelist maintained by runtime teams for known-good vendors or converter flags. Add 'compat-ack' registry that probe consults first.

Lena: Good idea. Compat-ack entries should include owner contact and allowed quirks. Probe will only auto-create triage issues if owner contact exists.

Ravi: Security note: don't allow probes to pull arbitrary external resources during static analysis. Only allow packaged model artifacts.

QA-bot: Quick reminder: please include unit tests for fingerprinting determinism and a flaky-test harness for microbench timing variance.

Lena: Action items:
- Omar: implement multiset-fingerprint prototype + tests (P0)
- Ravi: metrics and quota enforcement plan (P1)
- Priya: SDK dry-run + reproduce bundle design (P1)
- Lena: rollout advisory schedule and RFC patch (P0)

Ravi: +1 on timeline. I'll coordinate with infra to allocate a small GPU pool for microbenches.

Lena: I'll post the RFC update tomorrow and ping runtime owners for compat-ack entries. Thanks everyone.

bot-deploy: Created ticket INF-3301 to track probe alpha rollout. Assigned to Lena and Omar.

Priya: One more thought  we should include a 'why-to-fix' hint mapping in the triage issue, e.g., "try converter-x --no-op-fuse" for common op-fusing issues.

Lena: Noted; will include hints doc in RFC.
